gen-dafont-highway-gothic-fs-neco: Highway Gothic runs its strokes like bent pipe, friendly and unfussy from start to finish. And Neco brings a measured swell from hairline to stem, dignified where the heading is blunt.
gen-dafont-highway-gothic-fs-recia: Recia reads sharp but gentle, its text serif modulation showing only up close. Highway Gothic's constant-width strokes stand in front of it, and the two sit together like a drafting pen beside a fine nib.
gen-dafont-hiruko-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Hiruko draws pencil-like lines that never thicken or thin, with a moderate lowercase height that stays precise. Be Vietnam Pro then reads clean and smooth, its tall lowercase carrying the eye along.
gen-dafont-hiruko-fs-bespoke-sans: Hiruko has a signage-like plainness in every line, as if drawn with a single pencil. Bespoke Sans follows with generous space between curve ends and stems, so a long passage reads crisp and refined.
gen-dafont-hiruko-fs-erode: Erode reads editorial and dignified, with a tall middle band and a gentle ebb and flow in its serif strokes. But Hiruko's steel-cable lines hold flat, so a long passage moves from rigid to softly stamped.
gen-dafont-hiruko-fs-merriweather-sans: Merriweather Sans reads sturdy and large, its tall lowercase making words look broad and its e opening clearly to the right. Merriweather Sans handles the body text while Hiruko, monoline and precise, does its best work at the top of the page.
gen-dafont-hiruko-fs-neco: Hiruko's lowercase a has no thin hairlines at all, just one pencil-like line from edge to edge. And Neco, a text serif with the slight thickening of a reed pen, does its best work in the lines below.
gen-dafont-hiruko-fs-recia: Recia is a serif with light modulation you notice mostly up close, and its openings stay generous at every weight. Hiruko's flat strokes sit above it neatly.
gen-dafont-hiruko-lora: Lora feels literary, with a broad welcoming c. Hiruko draws flat, unswelling curves for crisp headings, while Lora's text serif swelling gives the body a gentle, bookish warmth.
gen-dafont-klill-archivo: Archivo has a commanding x-height and curves that open outward. Klill's pipe-cleaner letterforms and well-spaced curve endings give the pair a friendly, editorial directness that stays easy to follow.
